entry.title: Chancellor’s Medal
entry.content:
Agree & Join LinkedIn
        
  By clicking Continue to join or sign in, you agree to LinkedIn’s User Agreement, Privacy Policy, and Cookie Policy.

            Computer Scientist
        I’m excited to share that I was accepted for presentation at the International Conference on Artificial Life (ALIFE) 2025 in Kyoto, Japan.

My paper, “Growing Reservoirs with Developmental Graph Cellular Automata,” emerged from my Bachelor’s thesis under the supervision of Dr. James Stovold (co-author). The study proposes the unexplored idea of modeling nature’s purposeful growth based on function rather than form. In this case, that function is computation.

What is particularly interesting was the emergence of recurring, “life-like” reservoirs. This suggests that structure itself might play a more important role in computation than we’ve previously assumed. If that idea sparks your curiosity too, you can read more and access the paper on my project’s website (https://lnkd.in/eyHd2XPH).

A huge thank you to the #ALIFE2025 team for their organizational efforts. As a recent undergraduate, it was an incredible opportunity to be given a presentation slot among brilliant researchers from around the world. ALIFE’s uniquely interdisciplinary spirit makes this community so welcoming and every conversation so rich.

I’m also grateful to the incredible lineup of speakers, from Blaise Agüera y Arcas (CTO of Technology & Society at Google) to Emmett Shear (Former CEO of Twitch), and to all the poster presenters. Their talks left me inspired to continue exploring this field. entry.title: EASST award at ETAPS 2025
entry.content:

            Computer Scientist
        I am happy to share that the paper Unsatisfiability Proofs for Horn Solving I contributed to has won the EASST Award for the best ETAPS 2025 paper related to the systematic and rigorous engineering of software and systems.

My contributions focused on developing an extension for the “Golem” Horn solver to enable the generation of verifiable Alethe proofs, helping strengthen the reliability of software verification tools.

entry.title: Neptune Memorial Reef
entry.content:
The Neptune Memorial Reef is an underwater columbarium in what was conceived by Gary Levine as the world’s largest man-made reef, covering over 56,000 m2 of ocean floor at a depth of 12 m.

Curious spot-fin porcupinefish (Diodon hystrix) and school of unbothered snappers (Lutjanus).
Yellow stingray (Urobatis jamaicensis) and green moray (Gymnothorax funebris).

entry.title: LUComp travels to Bailrigg
entry.content:
Agree & Join LinkedIn
        
  By clicking Continue to join or sign in, you agree to LinkedIn’s User Agreement, Privacy Policy, and Cookie Policy.

            62 followers
        Last week, seven members from LU Leipzig’s Computer Science Society traveled to Bailrigg, England, to collaborate with their counterparts from the main campus: CompSoc. This visit was part of an international collaborative initiative that aims to strengthen ties between different Lancaster University campuses around the globe. Together, we worked on an ambitious project, an automatic waste sorting system, which continues the work started during a previous event in Leipzig: https://lnkd.in/eVNTTgGR

The event in Leipzig allowed both teams to bond while developing a prototype of a 3D-printed robotic arm in just three days! This time, though, we scaled things up. 💪 Instead of a single 3D-printed arm, we introduced two KUKA industrial robots, the same ones used in car assembly lines. These powerhouses, capable of handling loads of 180kg and moving at 3m/s, were crucial in elevating our solution to an industrial scale.

By dividing into sub-teams, we tackled the challenge with a combination of machine learning for object detection and classification, alongside robotics for precise sorting. We’re proud to say that this collaboration resulted in a promising proof-of-concept.

💡 By innovating in waste management, we hope to contribute toward sustainable solutions for one of the world’s growing environmental concerns. Our long-term vision is to extend this technology to more critical areas, such as nuclear waste management, where safe and efficient handling is of utter importance.

A huge thank you to all our collaborators and supporters! Special thanks go to:

LCSS’s team: Matias Barandiaran Rivera, Parichay Sachdev, Mustafa Azizi, Mikelis Kamepe, Osvaldo Catine Jr, Athar Syed and Inderjot Singh Litt.

CompSoc’s team: André Mariucci, Isaac R., Henry Oldroyd, Toby Vernon and Max.

Lancaster University Leipzig and Lancaster University.

Phil Benachour, Fabio Papacchini and Stephen Monk.

Together, we’re working toward a greener, more sustainable future, one innovative solution at a time. 🌱♻️

If you would like to see a quick demo, refer to our Github repository: https://lnkd.in/eeTV5AcTI help build resilient lives and businesses with proven methods - AI | Business Development |Accountability | Project Management | Marketing | SMEs | Team Building | Serving Startups, Legacies, & Leaders.Great Job guys! entry.title: Qiskit Fall Fest 2023
entry.content:
Agree & Join LinkedIn
        
  By clicking Continue to join or sign in, you agree to LinkedIn’s User Agreement, Privacy Policy, and Cookie Policy.

            Computer Scientist
        I am honored to share that I recently had the privilege of being the lead organizer for Lancaster University Leipzig's Qiskit Fall Fest 2023.

Qiskit, powered by IBM, is a robust Python library that empowers students and researchers to delve deeper into the practical aspects of the Quantum Computing (QC), enabling exploration at the circuit, pulse, and algorithm levels.

I would like to extend my gratitude to the following individuals and teams:

  • Parichay Sachdev, for his invaluable co-organizational efforts.
  • Ana Uznadze and Andrejs Bagdonas, for providing outstanding support during dynamic event sessions.
  • The team at Lancaster University Leipzig, for their valuable guidance and assistance.
  • Our esteemed panel of speakers: Aakash Ahmad, Dr Farina Riaz, and Enrique Solano, for taking time out of their busy schedules to generously contribute with insightful seminars.
  • The IBM team, whose vision made this opportunity a reality.

I remain motivated about the possibilities that QC brings to the table, and I hope that this initiative serves as an entry-point for students to explore it further. For more information on the event’s details, feel free to check out our official repository: https://lnkd.in/d5YjKMxR.Dear Matias Barandiarán Rivera, congratulations to you and your international team at Lancaster University Leipzig. Individual initiatives and leaderships like yours, with the dynamical creation of teams to organize successful events of this relevance, are the essence of progress measured as a creative expression of our artistic, scientific, technological, and entrepreneurial lives.
